title: Eutychus falls asleep and is revived — Acts 20
paragraphs: Eutychus falls asleep and is revived — Acts 20

He didn’t die in a brothel.
He died in church.
That’s what makes Acts 20 hit so hard.

Paul was preaching deep into the night. The room was crowded. The lamps were burning. The sermon kept going. And Eutychus, sitting on the window ledge, got drowsy… then dropped three stories and was picked up dead.

Imagine the silence.
The panic.
The guilt.
A young man crushed under the weight of one moment of weakness.
But Paul went down, threw himself over him, and said, “Do not be alarmed, for his life is in him” (Acts 20:10). And the boy was brought back alive.
And that’s where grace walks in.

Because Eutychus is more than a sleepy boy in a long sermon. He is us.
We sit near the window.
Close enough to hear truth… but still leaning toward the edge.
Tired. Distracted. Vulnerable. Nodding off in the very place where life is being spoken.
And sometimes our drift turns into a fall.

But here’s the Gospel: Jesus is not scared of fallen people. He comes down to where we crashed. He meets us in the ruin. He does not say, “You should have stayed awake.” He brings life where death had the final word.
That room in Acts 20 became a testimony that failure is not the end when Christ is near.

So if your soul feels drowsy… wake up.
If you’ve fallen… call on Jesus.
If you feel like you’ve gone too far down… grace still climbs stairs, reaches windows, and raises the broken.

There is hope for the tired.
There is mercy for the fallen.
There is life in Christ for those the world has already counted out.

Don’t confuse your fall with your finish.
Jesus still revives what sin, weakness, and weariness tried to bury.
